title: A Change at a Damascus School Has Syrians Reading the Runes
hook: A century after opening as a bastion of secularism, Damascus's prestigious Laique school has mandated sex-segregated classrooms, prompting Syrians to debate what the shift signals about their society's future.

title: How Italy's guiltiest food ritual went public
hook: Once frowned upon in polite dining rooms as an unrefined habit of the working class, 'fare la scarpetta'—wiping the plate clean with bread—has evolved into an Italian badge of culinary honor.

title: “Men with Queer Nerves”: The Jumping Frenchmen of Maine
hook: In the late 19th century, visitors to the Maine woods encountered French-Canadian lumberjacks with a bizarre condition that made them involuntarily leap, echo commands, and strike out at the slightest startle.

title: Ivan the Terrible Wanted to Marry Elizabeth I. How Did England's 'Virgin Queen' Reject the Russian Czar Without Souring Trade Relations?
hook: When Ivan the Terrible proposed marriage to Elizabeth I, the Virgin Queen faced a delicate geopolitical dilemma: turning down a volatile autocrat without tanking England's lucrative Russian trade.

title: Why did Stalin commit a robbery? The bloody heist that made the dictator’s name
hook: Long before ruling the Soviet Union, a young Stalin made his name by orchestrating a brazen, blood-soaked 1907 bank heist in Tiflis to bankroll the Bolshevik revolution.

title: Chinese Scam Boss Murdered in Sri Lanka Had Multiple Identities
hook: The brazen abduction and murder of a Chinese cybercrime syndicate leader in Sri Lanka reveals the network of shadow identities that enabled his cross-border scam operations.

title: Leaked files reveal how Deloitte Cyprus helped Roman Abramovich hide $10B fortune
hook: Leaked financial records expose how accounting giant Deloitte's Cyprus office backdated records and shuffled assets to help Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich shield a $10 billion fortune from sanctions.

title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
hook: In a stunning cybersecurity twist, federal investigators allege that executives at corporate ransomware negotiation firms were covertly operating the extortion infrastructure used by the ShinyHunters hacking ring.

title: An Ancient Virus Explains Why the Human Brain Is Special
hook: Millions of years ago, a prehistoric retrovirus silenced key brain-development genes across primate lineages, leaving ancestral humans uniquely untouched and altering our evolutionary trajectory.

title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
hook: After artificial intelligence produced a proof for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, human mathematicians finally unpacked its internal logic—revealing profound insights for number theory.

title: Ken Paxton Says He’s Tough on Crime. His Trust Invested $600,000 in a Convicted Fraudster’s Company.
hook: While campaigning on an unbending tough-on-crime platform, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton saw his blind trust quietly sink $600,000 into a venture founded by a convicted fraudster.

title: Traction!
hook: Friction is rarely noticed until it fails, but tribologists study how this ubiquitous contact force quietly governs everything from continental drift to microscopic machinery.

title: Mohammed Massoud Morsi on Writing About Palestinian Lives Beyond the Headlines
hook: Author Mohammed Massoud Morsi explores how literature can restore humanity and complexity to Palestinian life, creating space for personal narratives that transcend bleak headline statistics.

title: The rejuvenating secrets of the immortal jellyfish
hook: When injured, starved, or dying of old age, the tiny jellyfish Turritopsis dohrnii pulls off nature's ultimate reversal: transforming its mature cells back into youthful polyps to live all over again.

title: Pompeii wasn’t destroyed when you think it was
hook: For centuries, textbooks dated the catastrophic eruption of Mount Vesuvius to August 24, AD 79, but emerging archaeological evidence—from charcoal graffiti to autumnal harvests—points to an entirely different month.

title: The Alchemical Transformations of the Mutus Liber (1677)
hook: Published in 1677 without a single word of text, the enigmatic Mutus Liber attempted to guide initiates through the creation of the Philosopher’s Stone solely through cryptic, allegorical engravings.

title: Kremlin payment firm A7 has been pumping billions in ‘untraceable’ cash into global financial system
hook: Leaked banking records show how sanctioned payment firm A7 hauled over 280 tons of physical banknotes from Moscow markets to covertly pump billions into global finance.

title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
hook: British regulators have cracked down on Cryptomus, a shapeshifting payment processor unmasked as a critical laundering hub for international ransomware syndicates and dark web cartels.

title: Sanctioned Investor in Cambodian Scam Compound Owns California Mansion
hook: Even after being sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury for financing notorious cyber-scam compound operations in Cambodia, an international investor still holds a pristine $5 million mansion in California.

title: How Do Fungi Keep the Planet Healthy?
hook: Biologist Toby Kiers reveals how underground fungal networks function like sophisticated market traders, exchanging carbon and phosphorus with plant roots through ruthless biological haggling.

title: ‘It’s magic’: scientists rediscover how to make ancient Roman colour-changing glass
hook: Materials scientists have finally solved the 1,600-year-old riddle of the Roman Lycurgus Cup, reverse-engineering the ancient nanotech recipe that allows the glass chalice to shift color under light.

title: For the First Time, Scientists Trapped an Elusive Antimatter Particle—and Contained It for Months. It Could Allow Them to Test an Enduring Physics Theory
hook: Physicists have succeeded in trapping elusive antimatter particles for months at a time, opening the door to experiments that could finally explain why our matter-filled universe exists at all.

title: Horrible, unmanly, indispensable
hook: When firearms first spread across Renaissance Italy, knights and humanists decried them as unmanly 'devil's work'—until the brutal math of gunpowder warfare forced a total cultural surrender.

title: The Dominican Baseball Factory
hook: This hard-hitting investigation exposes the predatory shadow economy behind Major League Baseball in the Dominican Republic, where street-level scouts and moneylenders prey on prospects as young as 11.
